Title: AKU Provost opens the Network of Teaching & Learning's Scholarship of Teaching & Learning Inaugural Conference 2015
NewsSummary: AKU TL_net opens Scholarship of Teaching & Learning Inaugural Conference.
NewsContent:
On August 20, the AKU Network of Teaching and Learning (TL_net) held its first Scholarship of Teaching & Learning Inaugural Conference titled, Engaged Teaching for Engaged Learning.  Over 150 faculty in Karachi, Dar es Salaam, London and Nairobi took part both in person and virtually.

In his opening remarks the Provost reflected on his personal experience as a new young faculty member and the challenges he faced in the classroom - challenges that led him to understand the importance of teaching support of faculty.  This is the second time the Provost as been instrumental in setting up a unit for teaching and learning.  He pointed out the importance of having a place where faculty, especially ones new to the university, can get support services easily. 

The Provost congratulated the Director of the Networks of Quality, Teaching and Learning and the Network staff as well as AKU's faculty for their commitment to improvement in teaching and learning. The Provost said:

'In AKU's desire to be a student-centred "university of and for the developing world," TL_net is critical to the improvement of AKU's teaching and, thus, the success of our students in three very specific areas: (a) teaching and learning support; (b) promoting the scholarship of teaching and learning; and (c) evaluation, accountability and outreach on teaching and learning.'

Over the next two days, more than 60 faculty members will present posters and papers and will participate in workshops along with the other participants. Guest speakers, Prof Janet Welch from the University of Alberta and Prof Arshad Ahmad from McMaster University's Institute for Innovation and Excellence in Teaching & Learning (MIIETL), will give keynote addresses on various topics in the area of teaching and learning.
